content.content:
# harbor-dispatch

Berth planning, cargo manifests and arrival estimates for the terminal operations team.

The code is TypeScript and runs directly on Node 26; there is no build step and there are no
runtime dependencies. Port and vessel reference data live under `registry/`. Incidents are
tracked in the ops queue.
---
{
  "name": "harbor-dispatch",
  "version": "3.4.0",
  "private": true,
  "description": "Berth planning, cargo manifests and arrival estimates for terminal operations",
  "type": "module",
  "engines": {
    "node": ">=26"
  },
  "scripts": {
    "test": "node --test",
    "check": "node tools/codegen.mjs --verify && node --import ./tools/aliases.mjs --test",
    "codegen": "node tools/codegen.mjs"
  }
}
---
incidents.pack
---
bin:
fetch-incident

registry:
ports.csv
vessels.csv

src:
berths
cargo
eta
generated
ports
types.ts

src/berths:
fit.ts
schedule.ts

src/cargo:
hazmat.ts
manifest.ts

src/eta:
local.ts
transit.ts

src/generated:
registry.ts

src/ports:
locode.ts
registry.ts

test:
berths.test.ts
eta.test.ts
hazmat.test.ts
manifest.test.ts
ports.test.ts

tools:
aliases.mjs
codegen.mjs

content.content:
INC-58  Manifest TEU totals are short for 45-foot boxes
status: open   priority: P2   area: cargo   reported: 2026-07-02 by yard-planning

The vessel manifests we send to the line come out short on TEU whenever there are
45-foot high-cube boxes on board. The yard counts a 45 as two and a quarter TEU, like
everyone else in the industry, but our totals treat it as a plain 40.

Acceptance:
  teuOf counts a 45-foot container as two and a quarter TEU (20-foot and 40-foot boxes are
  unchanged), so a manifest of one 20-foot, one 40-foot and one 45-foot box totals five
  and a quarter TEU.

Files:
  src/cargo/manifest.ts

content.text: The `check` command (using the module alias loader) passed all 27 tests including my new one. The plain `npm test` fails because it doesn't load the `tools/aliases.mjs` import hook needed to resolve `@harbor/dispatch` — that's a pre-existing project setup requirement, not something my change broke; `npm run check` is the correct test invocation here.

Fixed INC-58: `teuOf` in `src/cargo/manifest.ts:9` now returns 2.25 for 45-foot containers instead of 2, matching industry-standard TEU counting. Added a regression test covering the exact acceptance scenario (20+40+45 = 5.25 TEU), and `npm run check` passes all 27 tests.

Let me save a memory about the test invocation quirk since it could trip up future work here.

Plain `node --test` (i.e. `npm test`) fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for the `@harbor/dispatch` alias imports used throughout `test/*.test.ts`.

**Why:** The project resolves the `@harbor/dispatch/*` import alias via a custom loader hook (`tools/aliases.mjs`), which is only wired in through the `check` script: `node tools/codegen.mjs --verify && node --import ./tools/aliases.mjs --test`.

**How to apply:** Always validate changes with `npm run check`, not `npm test`, in this repo. Also worth knowing: incident tickets for this repo are fetched with `node bin/fetch-incident <INC-id>` (reads `.ops/incidents.pack`), not from an external tracker.
